page_title: Clojure hands-on tutorial for beginners: building a spell-checker

summary.title: Clojure hands-on tutorial for beginners: building a spell-checker
summary.one_liner: You learn basic Clojure by building a working command-line spell checker with Leiningen, using a word list, set operations, and Levenshtein edit distance from Apache Commons.
takeaways: Build a command-line spell checker that reports whether a word is correct and suggests the closest dictionary word.
Use Clojure sets and a word list to check membership, cleaning entries with clojure.string/trim via map.
Compute Levenshtein edit distance by reusing Apache Commons Lang3 from Java inside Clojure, declared in project.clj.
Pick the closest match with min-key, using partial to fix one argument and apply to run it over the word list.
Ways to improve it: a bigger or better word list, and weighting suggestions by word probability as Peter Norvig describes.
summary.summary: The author walks the reader through building a spell checker in Clojure, step by step, with hidden solutions to exercises so readers can try first. The project is created with Leiningen, and the dictionary is loaded from a downloaded English word list with slurp, split into lines, cleaned and turned into a set. Core Clojure ideas such as defn, if, let, partial and apply are introduced as they are needed. Suggestions come from Levenshtein edit distance, taken from Apache Commons Lang3 and picked with min-key. The tutorial closes with ideas for improving the word list and similarity measure.
